# BitChord 1.0.4
## Automix
- Beat detection now runs on the Neural Engine through Core ML. It is about four to five times faster on Apple Silicon and closer to the original model than before. Short tracks, and anything the Neural Engine can't take, fall back to the CPU. - Both Automix models, the beat tracker and the vocal detector, are now optional downloads that are verified on the device. The app no longer bundles the vocal model, so it is smaller. BitChord offers them at launch and in Settings. Without them, Automix uses its built-in fallbacks. - When a tempo glide ends, the waveform phase stays put. Tempo-aligned stretches keep stereo phase, and the bass in a transition is no longer lost. - Analysis work is capped in CPU and memory, and stale analysis is cancelled.
## Search
- A new **Library** source sits beside YouTube and Addons. It filters your signed-in library (songs, artists, albums, playlists) and the music on this device as you type, without network requests. - **iPad:** a round search button grows into the search field. In portrait, the source switcher moves under the top bar. - **Mac:** the search field, source switcher, account and Downloads sit in order in the title bar, and switching source re-runs the search.
## iPad
- iPad now uses the system's adaptable sidebar, as Music does. It holds a Playlists section with Liked Music first, and the account and Settings at its foot. - Each tab keeps a page history, with back and forward buttons beside the logo (and ⌘[ / ⌘]). - The playback pill is capped at the mini-player width. In portrait, the volume row lines up with the Lyrics and Up Next buttons.
## iPhone
- The player pill tucks into the minimized tab bar while you scroll, and rides above the keyboard.
## Playback and sources
- Lossless streams are used whenever the quality setting is Lossless, whatever the output. As upstream does, Bluetooth only sidelines addons that require a lossless-capable output. - Lossless sources are preferred before playback starts, and completed quality upgrades are confirmed. BitChord checks decoded formats, and interrupted playback recovers with a capped number of retries. - Playback sessions are kept across restarts. Source lists survive storage read failures, and each source shows its check and renewal state. - The JioSaavn catalogue and playback work again. - Addon session renewal is opt-in and uses provider links you supply. - Normalization headroom is back in Transparent playback, and explicit gapless repeat works. - Audio settings now separate the requested quality, the measured output and the processing. The quality status is clearer, and the diagnostics refresh live.
## Offline and downloads
- Downloads show per-song progress and pending states. - Cached and downloaded songs keep their artwork, and covers come back after launch without network requests. Offline playback is kept.
## Fixes
- Mac: the player's back button responds across its full visible area, and a crash in Settings is fixed. - Videos start faster. - Leaks during audio engine and interpreter teardown are fixed. - The Liquid Glass icon draws its waves at full size. - Version & Updates compares both version and build, and offers the installer for your platform.

# BitChord 1.0.3
## Sound
- Automix blends no longer open with a hissy stretch where neither song has its kick or bass line. The next song's low end now arrives as the previous song lets go of its own. - Removed a tiny skip, about 3 ms, that came once in each Automix song shortly after the blend. - Tempo matching during a blend is smoother on dense, bass-heavy records, uses about half the processing power, and lets go of the tempo sooner after the blend. Tempo differences too small to hear are no longer matched at all.

# BitChord 1.0.2
## Playback
- Playback no longer stops when a song can't be played. BitChord now tries several other ways to get the song first, including the same recording from another catalogue you have enabled. Only if all of them fail does it skip to the next song, which it prepares in advance so Automix still blends into it. - A song that fails to load no longer stalls the queue. Autoplay and Automix now carry on to the next song. - Moving the seek bar while Automix is blending two songs now jumps within the song you're hearing. Before, playback could go silent until the app was restarted. - When YouTube asks your network to confirm it isn't a bot, BitChord now says so plainly and pauses its requests, instead of reporting every song as unplayable.
## Sound
- Removed the crackle and hiss on kicks and bass in loud tracks. The default Transparent mode now gently turns down peaks that would go over full scale, instead of clipping them. Everything below full scale plays exactly as before. - Automix raises a quieter next song by at most 2 dB, down from 6 dB, so blends don't overload loud masters. - On iPhone and iPad, AirPods and other route changes no longer make playback stutter.
## Discord
- Signing in to Discord now captures the session reliably, and the "Listening to" status reconnects on its own after sleep or a network change.
## Addons
- Addon URLs keep their configured paths. - On iOS, you can now remove an addon by swiping it, with a confirmation step. - Better compatibility with addons: resource manifests, extra metadata field names, and streams that can't be played are declined cleanly.
Thanks to [@Daltonganger](https://github.com/Daltonganger) for the addon fixes in [#2](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/pull/2), [#3](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/pull/3) and [#4](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/pull/4).
## Requirements
- macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon. - iOS or iPadOS 18 or later.
## Downloads and installation
- **Mac:** Apple Silicon DMG. It is ad-hoc signed, not notarized, and not Developer ID signed. Macs already running 1.0.1 can update from within the app. - **iOS:** Unsigned IPA for sideloading with AltStore, SideStore, or Sideloadly, or for signing with your own Apple Developer team.
### Install on Mac
Drag BitChord to Applications, then open it. If Gatekeeper blocks the first launch, use either route:
- **System Settings:** Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, choose **Open Anyway** for BitChord, then confirm **Open** in the warning dialog. - **Terminal:** After moving BitChord to Applications, run:
```sh xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/BitChord.app" open "/Applications/BitChord.app" ```
### Sideload on iPhone or iPad
1. Install AltStore, SideStore, or Sideloadly and connect the device as required by that tool. 2. Import the unsigned IPA and sign it with your Apple account or developer team. 3. Install the signed app and trust the developer profile if iOS asks.
To use iCloud lyrics-choice or sign-in sharing, sign the app with your own team and enable the matching iCloud Key-Value Store and iCloud Keychain capabilities and provisioning profile. Otherwise those features use local device storage.
## Legal
BitChord does not host or provide media. Playback uses configured third-party services and their APIs; availability and terms are controlled by those services. See the [README Disclaimer & Legal Notice](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/blob/v1.0.2/README.md#disclaimer--legal-notice).
Every GitHub release is built from its tagged commit, and that tag's source archive is the Corresponding Source under GPLv3 §6. The source for this release is the [v1.0.2 tag](https://github.com/bagumamartin/BitChord/tree/v1.0.2).
